title: Dryer, clipper and equipment safety
audience: Mobile pet groomers who use dryers, clippers, blades and electrical equipment at a client's home or venue
referencesAtStart: Official source: WorkSafe Victoria, Protecting health and safety at work: health and safety responsibilities (reviewed 3 April 2025), for the self-employed and employer duties.
learningOutcomes: Inspect dryers, clippers, blades and cables before each groom, and remove any unsafe item from use
Use dryers and clippers so that heat, noise and moving parts do not harm the animal or the groomer
Apply the confirmed Victorian WHS duty for self-employed people to the equipment and the client's home

instruction.heading: Inspect before every groom
instruction.body: Grooming equipment is used close to an animal's skin, eyes and feet, and close to the groomer's hands. Inspect each item before the first groom of the day. Check the dryer for a cracked housing, a loose nozzle, a fan that is noisy or stiff, and a damaged cord or plug. Check each clipper for a cracked body, a loose blade, a blade that is blunt, and a cord that is frayed or taped. Check the blade for heat after use, and for blunt or chipped teeth. Check the anchor point for any restraint in use. Remove any item that fails, label it, and record the removal on the equipment record. The business's inspection checklist is held in {{business:equipment.inspection_checklist}}, and the manufacturer's instructions are in {{business:equipment.manufacturer_manual_url}}.

instruction.heading: Heat, noise and moving parts
instruction.body: A dryer produces hot air and noise. Keep the nozzle moving and never hold it on one spot, because heat builds on the skin quickly. Start on the lowest heat and speed that dry the coat, and check the skin of the animal and your own hand for heat. Never leave a dryer running unattended, and never dry an animal in an enclosed space with no ventilation. Clippers have a moving blade and can heat up during long use. Let them cool between animals, and clean them as the manufacturer directs. Keep a grip on the animal when a blade is near the face, ears, feet or tail. Use hearing protection if the noise is high for long periods.

instruction.heading: Electrical safety at a client's home
instruction.body: A mobile groomer depends on a power outlet the client provides. Check the outlet, the cable and the load before plugging in, as “Mobile setup, power and wet-area safety” explains. Keep cords off the floor where the animal or the groomer could trip, and keep electrical equipment away from water. WorkSafe Victoria's responsibilities page (reviewed 03/04/2025) says a self-employed person must manage their work so that it does not put others' health and safety at risk, to the extent that is reasonably practicable. The same page extends the employer's duty to the people a business's work reaches, such as clients and the general public. Treat the home as one for set-up and safety, and record the set-up check. Where equipment is damaged or wet, switch it off and do not use it until it has been checked by a competent person.

procedure: Inspect each dryer, clipper, blade and cord before the first groom, and record the check
Remove any unsafe item from use, label it, and record the removal
Check the outlet, cable and load before plugging in, and keep cords clear of walkways
Keep the dryer nozzle moving, start on the lowest heat and speed, and check the animal's skin for heat
Let clippers cool between animals, and keep a grip on the animal when the blade is near sensitive areas
Switch off and remove from use any equipment that is damaged or wet, and record the action

workedExamples.situation: A groomer finds that a clipper cord has a split in the insulation near the plug, but the clipper still runs. The groomer plans to tape the split and use the clipper for the day.
workedExamples.reasoning: A split cord is an unsafe item, and taping it does not make it safe. The clipper must be removed from use and not used until it has been repaired or replaced by a competent person. The groomer should record the removal, and use a second clipper if one is safe. The WorkSafe duty for self-employed people applies to the groom, so the unsafe item must not be used.

workedExamples.situation: A dog is being dried, and the groomer holds the dryer on the dog's back in one spot for several minutes because the coat is thick.
workedExamples.reasoning: Holding hot air on one spot can burn the skin, and the groomer should keep the nozzle moving. The groomer should stop, check the skin for heat, let the area cool, and continue with the nozzle moving at a lower heat. The groomer should record the incident if the skin is affected, and check the dryer's settings.

equipmentAndPpe: Dryer with a moving nozzle and a lowest-heat setting
Clippers with blades checked for sharpness and heat
Hearing protection where the noise is high for long periods
Gloves for handling clippers and animals
Cable and outlet check tools, including a portable tester where the business supplies one

commonErrors.error: Using a clipper with a split cord because it still works.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the clipper from use. Taping a split cord does not make it safe.

commonErrors.error: Holding a dryer on one spot for a long time.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the nozzle moving and check the skin for heat.
Never leave a dryer running unattended. Switch it off when stepping away.

commonErrors.error: Stating that the noise and heat limits for grooming equipment are confirmed.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the limits.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria's responsibilities page (reviewed 03/04/2025) states the self-employed duty and the employer duty to other people the work reaches. Those duties are confirmed for Victoria.
WorkSafe does not say this directly.
Noise and heat limits for grooming equipment were not researched. The manufacturer's instructions apply.
Completing this lesson does not grant any electrical licence or authority to carry out electrical work at a client's premises.

qualityStandard: Every dryer, clipper, blade and cord is inspected before the first groom, and the check is recorded
No damaged or wet equipment is used, and every removal is recorded
Every dryer use keeps the nozzle moving, with the skin checked for heat
Every client outlet is checked before the equipment is plugged in
documentationEvidence: Equipment inspection record, with the date and the items checked
Removed-from-use record for each unsafe item, with the date and reason
Set-up checklist for each visit, including the outlet check
Incident record for any burn, cut, shock or equipment fault
summary: Inspect dryers, clippers, blades and cords before each groom
Keep dryers moving and check the skin for heat; let clippers cool
Remove damaged or wet equipment from use; taping a split cord is not a fix
Completing this lesson grants no electrical licence or authority
referencesAtEnd: Official source, as listed at the start.

knowledgeChecks.question: A clipper cord has a split in the insulation, but the clipper still runs. What is the correct action?
options: Tape the split and use the clipper for the rest of the day, since the tape holds the cord
Remove the clipper from use until it is repaired or replaced, and record the removal
Use the clipper only on short-coated animals, since the cord is safe then

knowledgeChecks.question: A groomer is drying a dog and holds the dryer on one spot for several minutes. What should the groomer do?
options: Keep going, since the coat is thick and needs the heat to dry through
Increase the heat to dry the spot faster before the next dog is ready
Keep the nozzle moving, let the skin cool if it is warm, and check it

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the WHS reference this lesson uses, how far must a self-employed person manage risk to others?
options: To the extent that is reasonably practicable
Only where a client makes a complaint
Not at all inside a client's home
